visual.general_description: Four-panel composite (A-D) of axial lung-window chest CT slices photographed from a display, each labelled in a dark box and marked with black arrows, showing bilateral hazy lung opacities, then a large air-filled cavity in the left-sided posterior lung, a much smaller residual cavity, and finally no visible cavity.
visual.detailed_description: Two-by-two grid, 750 x 524 px, panels A (top left), B (top right), C (bottom left) and D (bottom right), each with a dark letter box at upper left. A shows bilateral patchy peripheral consolidative/hazy opacities with two arrows and no cavity. B shows a large sharply demarcated posterior air-filled cavity in the image-right (conventionally patient left) lung with one arrow, plus diffuse hazy bilateral opacities. C shows a small thin-walled cavity in the same posterior lung region with one arrow and otherwise mostly clear lungs. D, at a lower slice level, shows no cavity at the arrowed site and only subtle hazy posterior-basal changes. The panels are photographs of a monitor (stripe/moire artifacts) with no legible patient identifiers, dates, L/R markers or scale bars.

panels.general_description: Axial lung-window chest CT slice with bilateral patchy hazy and consolidative peripheral lung opacities and two black arrows, without a visible cavity.
panels.detailed_description: Dark box labelled "A" at upper left. Axial slice at an upper-to-mid thoracic level with a single round central airway lumen in front of the spine. The lung on the image-left side shows patchy hazy increased attenuation and denser consolidation extending from the lateral and posterior periphery toward the hilum, with air-filled bronchi and vessels visible within it. The lung on the image-right side is mostly dark and aerated centrally, with a faint hazy peripheral opacity near the posterolateral margin and a hazy posterior basal region. One black arrow points at the posterolateral peripheral opacity of the image-left lung and a second black arrow points at the posterolateral peripheral opacity of the image-right lung. No round or oval air-containing lesion with its own wall is seen in this slice.

panels.general_description: Axial lung-window chest CT slice with a large well-demarcated air-filled cavity in the dependent left-sided (image-right) lung marked by a black arrow, with patchy bilateral hazy opacities.
panels.detailed_description: Dark box labelled "B" at upper left. Axial slice at the level of the central airways, with two central airway lumina and the heart/great vessels in the mediastinum. The image-right lung contains a large, sharply demarcated, black oval air-filled lucency in the posterior dependent portion, with a comparatively straight posterior margin and denser soft-tissue-density lung/pleural opacity along its posterior and lateral edge. A black arrow from the lower right points at its posterolateral margin. Both lungs show diffuse patchy hazy (ground-glass-like) opacities, more conspicuous peripherally in the image-left lung, with visible vessels. A small white computer cursor arrow is visible near the chest wall at the right edge of the image.

panels.general_description: Axial lung-window chest CT slice with mostly clear lungs and a small thin-walled air-containing cavity in the posterior image-right lung marked by a black arrow.
panels.detailed_description: Dark box labelled "C" at upper left. Axial slice at the level of the carina/main bronchi, with two round central airway lumina. Both lungs are largely dark and well aerated with thin branching vessels. In the posterior image-right lung, a small oval air-containing cavity with a thin wall is marked by a black arrow from below; a tiny bright focus lies along its posterior wall. A small ill-defined hazy nodular opacity is present in the anterior-upper image-left lung, and faint hazy peripheral changes lie laterally in the image-right lung. A small half-black/half-white circular icon is visible at the left margin of the image. The residual cavity is much smaller than the cavity in panel B.
